summary: Specifies NFILE, a file access protocol, along with the underlying Token List Transport Layer and Byte Stream with Mark. The goal is to promote discussion and encourage designers of future file protocols to adopt its ideas. It is now historic.

eli5.summary: It is a way to open, read and save files on another computer as if they were on yours, with the design shared so others can learn from it.

questions: how does the nfile protocol work
what operating systems did nfile support
subtitle: A layered file access protocol for remote file operations

tldr.problem: Accessing files on remote computers required a robust protocol that could handle diverse operating systems, support partial file transfers, and recover gracefully from interruptions.
tldr.mechanism: NFILE is a layered protocol where file commands are encoded as token lists and transmitted over control connections, with data flowing on separate channels. A Token List Transport Layer and Byte Stream with Mark provide reliable structured communication.
tldr.outcome: NFILE enables transparent file operations across heterogeneous systems and was implemented on Symbolics machines and UNIX servers. It is now historic.

today: RFC 1037 is now Historic. NFILE was successfully deployed between Symbolics machines and on UNIX servers, but is no longer actively used. The protocol exemplified important design principles for distributed file systems that influenced later work, and demonstrated how to build portable systems using layered protocol design.

sections.title: NFILE and Remote File Access
sections.content:
NFILE stands for New File Protocol, replacing an earlier protocol named QFILE. It was designed at Symbolics and enables a client program to perform file operations on a remote host, including reading and writing entire files, accessing parts of files, deleting, renaming, creating links, and listing directories.

NFILE was successfully used between Symbolics machines since 1985 and has been implemented on UNIX hosts as well. It is designed to work with any file system, not just native Symbolics storage. The protocol version defined here is user version 2 and server version 2, with extensibility planned for future requirements.
sections.eli5: NFILE lets a computer ask another computer to open, read, change, and delete files as if they were on the first computer. It works between different kinds of computers running different systems.

sections.title: Layered Protocol Architecture
sections.content:
NFILE is built in layers. At the top, client programs or user interfaces call NFILE. Below NFILE sits the Token List Transport Layer, which transmits simple structured data (like lists). Below that is Byte Stream with Mark, which provides an out-of-band signal for user interruptions. At the bottom is a reliable byte-transmission protocol, currently TCP or Chaosnet.

This layering gives NFILE portability: any byte stream can be used as the foundation. Token lists are NFILE's way of encoding commands and responses as sequences of keywords, numbers, and strings. All commands go over a single control connection, while file data flows on separate data channels for input (server to client) and output (client to server).
sections.eli5: NFILE is built like a sandwich: the file commands on top, then a layer that sends structured data, then a layer for handling interruptions, then the actual network at the bottom. Each layer does its job, and the whole thing works on any network that can send bytes reliably.

sections.title: File Operations and Commands
sections.content:
NFILE supports a comprehensive set of commands. The OPEN command opens a file for reading, writing, or direct access. The CLOSE command closes a file. READ and DIRECT-OUTPUT request data to flow, DELETE removes a file, and RENAME changes its name. The DIRECTORY command lists files with optional filters and properties.

Each command gets a unique transaction identifier (up to 15 characters), generated by the client. The server is not required to answer commands in the order received, so the transaction identifier links each response to the right command. Notifications from the server can also arrive asynchronously on the control connection to report events or errors.
sections.eli5: The client and server exchange commands by name, like OPEN to open a file and CLOSE to close it. Every command gets a label (a transaction identifier) so the client can match up the server's answers with what it asked for.

sections.title: Data Stream and Direct Access Modes
sections.content:
NFILE supports two ways of transferring file data. Data stream mode (the default) transfers an entire file as a continuous stream. The client gives the OPEN command, the file is opened on the server, and data immediately flows over a data channel until it is complete. This mode is simple and efficient for whole-file transfers.

Direct access mode enables reading or writing from a specific position in a file. The client opens a file with a direct file identifier, then issues individual READ commands to request data from a specific byte position, or DIRECT-OUTPUT commands to write from a position. The FILEPOS command can set the write position. This mode allows random access to large files without transferring the whole file.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to get a file: get the whole thing at once (data stream), or ask for just the parts you need from wherever you want them (direct access), like skipping to the middle of a book and reading from there.

sections.title: Robustness and Resynchronization
sections.content:
A key design goal was handling user aborts gracefully. If a connection or channel is disrupted (for example, by an interrupt signal), the protocol cannot recover unless both sides know they are in a safe state. NFILE includes a resynchronization procedure using a special mark signal (sent via Byte Stream with Mark) to bring a disrupted control connection or data channel back into a known state. After resynchronization, the connection can be reused.

NFILE also handles character set translation. The protocol defines an extended ASCII character set, and servers on systems with different native character sets (UNIX, TOPS-20, VMS, or Symbolics) translate characters as needed. Three translation modes are provided: NORMAL (the default, ensuring round-trip integrity), RAW (no translation), and SUPER-IMAGE (for PDP-10 systems only). The protocol carefully distinguishes between NFILE units (character positions) and server units to avoid confusion during direct access.
sections.eli5: When something goes wrong and the connection breaks, NFILE can send a special signal to both sides saying "start over from a known good place", so the connection can be used again. The protocol also handles translating letters and characters from one computer's way of storing them to another's.
